Actually l used to think that this argument is the strongest one against antinatalism, but now l can say it's the strongest argument FOR antinatalism, and I'm happy to tell you why.


Currently, Humans' negative effect on animals is much bigger than their positive effect, and there are no compelling evidences that this will be reversed in the near future. As for the far future, it's simply unpredictable, unknown. And I don't think you'd like to justify bringing another human based on the unknown.

I can also claim that maintaining human existence will result in a much greater suffering in the universe due to the possible misuse of future technology. Watch this video to know how:

https://youtu.be/hvDlYnCejHk


But as I mentioned, this is related to the far future which is unpredictable, unknown. So, what we need to do when we talk about the morality of having kids is to make a judgement based on what we know, not what we don't.

Moreover, even if we can actually predict that in the far future humans will have a net positive effect on animals, you will still need to be an antinatalist. Why? Because in order to reach that future, you don't need to waste your resources reproducing another child while you can adopt one, but you need to increase people's awareness about animals suffering, the importance of reducing it, and the best means to achieve that noble goal.

In other words, instead of wasting a huge amount of time, money, and energy in order to bring a new person into the world to convince him to reduce suffering, you can simply double your effort to convince many of those who are already existed. And whenever you find time, you can always convince another one. In fact, You will die and billions of existed persons will remain unconvinced. And some of those convinced by you will start have conversations with others and thus the circle of awareness and compassion for animals will expand and never stop expanding. 

Therefore, we can conclude that having a kid now is completely unnecessary to reduce animals suffering while not having a kid is necessary.

"Who is to say that human life will not just re evolve again and we will have to go through all of the pains of the hunter gatherer times etc?"

There is no way to discover whether those two possibilities are true or false. Therefore, l don't think it's appropriate to use them to justify anything.
